title: Energy R5C cleaner historical event case and evaluation grammar

case.why: Issuer April 9 invitation states consensus is published one week before April 30 results; current historical archive labels Q1 2025 as collected April 2025 with 20 analyst inputs. No independent pre-event byte/timestamp for the exact panel was recovered. Same-day results were not paired with a Capital Markets Update, but the release contained a new buyback tranche and additional Empire Wind exposure/context; Empire Wind halt itself was already public from April 17.

evaluation_spec.default_return_window: For before-open results, prior official close to event-day official close; for after-close results, event-day close to next trading-day close. Always record local exchange timezone and source.
evaluation_spec.benchmark_rule: Use a declared investable/local broad benchmark for descriptive residuals; do not call stock-minus-index alpha.
evaluation_spec.commodity_rule: Preserve relevant commodity changes as separate context unless a predeclared calibrated exposure model exists; do not subtract Brent or TTF one-for-one from the stock return.
evaluation_spec.metric_rule: Consensus and actual must share metric definition, unit, period and ownership scope before surprise is computed.
evaluation_spec.panel_rule: Contributor count, aggregation method and panel turnover travel with each estimate; aggregate changes do not prove matched-analyst revisions.
evaluation_spec.horizon_rule: Estimate revisions require the same fixed fiscal horizon; rollover into a new forecast year is not revision evidence.
evaluation_spec.corporate_action_rule: Adjust mechanical ex-dividend/split/rights effects in return construction; announcements of buybacks/financing are event information and belong in the confound ledger.
evaluation_spec.confound_rule: Inventory earnings, guidance, strategy/CMD, M&A, financing/capital return, policy/regulation, commodity/macro shocks and corporate actions. Confounded events may inform descriptive grammar but cannot train a clean causal earnings-surprise rule without explicit treatment.
evaluation_spec.lookahead_rule: Every input must have first-known time <= decision cutoff; later archive corrections/restatements remain later vintages.
evaluation_spec.rights_rule: Public access is not commercial ingestion/redistribution permission; rights/admission remain with existing evidence owners.
evaluation_spec.predictive_rule: No predictive/alpha claim until event definitions, sample construction, controls and holdout are frozen before evaluation and pass accepted out-of-sample testing.

acceptance_cases: Do not label an exact panel value PRE_EVENT_TIMESTAMPED when only issuer process plus a current archive supports it.
Do not use result-morning third-party reporting to backdate exact consensus bytes to a week earlier.
Require metric-definition matching; adjusted net income cannot substitute for adjusted operating income after tax.
Preserve mixed surprise vectors rather than one generic beat/miss bit.
Before-open and after-close releases use different declared return windows.
A reported same-day stock change is not a reproduced return series.
Stock-minus-index is descriptive residual, not alpha.
Do not subtract commodity percentage moves one-for-one from equity returns.
Empire Wind halt remains pre-known from April 17; later result detail is separate event information.
Northern Lights Phase 2 FID remains pre-known from March 27.
Same-day buyback tranche belongs to event confounds but is not a mechanical ex-date adjustment.
No ex-dividend adjustment is applied on April 30 when the stated Q1 dividend ex-date is in August.
Panel sample changes must not be labelled within-analyst estimate revision.
Forecast-year rollover is not estimate revision.
Historical archive retrieval time and historical estimate first-known time remain distinct.
Later restatements do not overwrite the original event information set.
Confounded events cannot be treated as clean causal labels without an explicit treatment.
A cleaner event relative to Q4 is not automatically a clean event.
One historical case cannot establish predictive edge.
Research never changes ranking, entry, sizing or trading authority.
